correctness.rationale: The exact exponent criterion follows directly from \(\tau(n)=\prod_i(a_i+1)\): if \(n\) has exact support \(S\), every prime dividing every \(a_i+1\) must lie in \(S\), and the \(p_j\)-valuation of \(\tau(n)\) is the column sum \(\sum_i e_{ij}\), which must not exceed \(a_j\). Conversely those conditions imply \(\tau(n)\mid n\). For fixed \(S\), the count of \(S\)-smooth integers up to \(y\) is the lattice-point volume \(C_S(\log y)^m+O((\log y)^{m-1})\). With \(L=\log x\) and \(T=\log L\), independently bounding each \(A_i=a_i+1\) from above and below shows that tuples obeying only the size condition number \(C_S^mT^{m^2}(1+o(1))\). Each exponent coordinate \(e_{ij}=O(T)\); hence a tuple can violate a column inequality only if some \(A_j=O(T)\), a set of size \(O(T^{m(m-1)}(\log T)^m)=o(T^{m^2})\). Fresh exact checks of the structural criterion on supports \(\{2\},\{2,3\},\{2,5\},\{2,3,5\}\) agreed with direct divisibility in every tested exponent box.
residual_risks: The support is fixed; no uniformity is claimed when its size or primes vary with \(x\).
The proof supplies a leading asymptotic only, not an optimized error term.

originality.rationale: Colton's complete primary article defines refactorable numbers, develops membership constructions, and in its distribution section counts refactorable integers having a prescribed divisor count. It does not count refactorable integers with a prescribed exact prime support. Spiro's 1985 work is a global counting theorem over all supports. The audited fixed-support asymptotic lives on a different logarithmic scale and requires an \(m^2\)-dimensional smooth-exponent lattice plus a proof that the valuation-column constraints remove only lower-order mass. Current Resultary searches returned the assigned theorem first and no stronger fixed-support result.

value.rationale: Exact prime support is a standard and useful way to stratify sparse multiplicative sets. The theorem converts the divisibility condition into a transparent exponent-lattice model and determines the exact leading constant on every finite support. This gives a natural local asymptotic complementary to the classical global count.
